OpenHubForAI

The Open*Hubs (22)

The open ecosystem both Teleon and Baltor consume. Each hub is continuously populated (discover · generate · intake), governed, and verify-gated.

OpenContextHub

Governed, source-handled context packs (Knowledge Corpus) you drop into a capability without re-curating provenance.

e.g. Pull a verified context pack with source handles for a RAG step

OpenSkillsHub

A registry of reusable agent skills (SKILL.md procedures) for specialized workflows, with provenance.

e.g. Install a ready SKILL.md procedure instead of writing the workflow

OpenToolsHub

Tools and agnostic capability planes (OCR, search, browser…) behind one uniform interface, swappable by registry.

e.g. Drop in the OCR plane's components for a document pipeline

OpenSkillToTool

Compile a fuzzy agent skill into a deterministic, typed tool — and back — to remove an LLM call.

e.g. Promote a proven skill into a deterministic typed tool

OpenHubForAI

The open evals, harnesses, templates, and CapabilityTask spec the whole ecosystem builds on.

e.g. Pull the web_browsing ladder (API→browser→stealth) for an acquisition step

OpenMCPHub

MCP servers and their advertised tools, indexed as governed components an agent can consume.

e.g. Discover an MCP server's tools as typed components

OpenCompressionHub

Reversible context-compression policies that fit a token budget without dropping answer-critical facts.

e.g. Apply a reversible compression policy to fit a context window

OpenBenchmarkHub

Per-capability benchmark cards + datasets to score candidate execution graphs on real metrics, not vibes.

e.g. Score a candidate DAG against a capability's benchmark dataset

OpenReviewHub

Review-routing rules and verdicts that send low-confidence work to the right human or panel.

e.g. Route a low-confidence change to human review automatically

OpenTemplatesHub

Reusable DAG and object templates you mutate with a vertical's components instead of designing from zero.

e.g. Start from the provider_directory template for a new vertical

OpenEndpointHub

Inference lane profiles + endpoint prices to simulate and cost a DAG before you run it.

e.g. Simulate a DAG's cost from real lane prices

OpenEnvironmentHub

Runnable agent-eval environments + executable reward specs to score candidate DAGs (evidence, never promotion authority).

e.g. Score a candidate DAG in a runnable eval environment

OpenSandboxHub

Isolated execution sandboxes with risk/conformance profiles for running candidate code safely (sandbox output never truth).

e.g. Run candidate code in a conformance-passing sandbox

OpenAgentHub

The agent runtimes that run agents — bounded adapters + run-receipt shapes (agents propose, never serve truth).

e.g. Pick a bounded agent-runtime adapter for a task

OpenReceiptHub

Portable, signed receipts (AI-BOM) a served fact or run carries so it verifies anywhere.

e.g. Attach a portable signed receipt to a served fact

OpenStateHub

Governed persistent agent state (memory / blackboard / graph) shapes for durable working state (analytical, never auto-served).

e.g. Persist durable agent working state in a governed blackboard shape

OpenRoutingHub

Reliability-weighted model-routing policy — the cheapest viable provider for a model, not the default frontier.

e.g. Pick the cheapest sufficient + reliable provider for a model call

OpenReconciliationHub

The Reconcile method — merge conflicting records into one canonical candidate, lineage preserved.

e.g. Reconcile conflicting source records into a canonical candidate

OpenHardeningHub

The Harden method — pass a candidate against schema and policy gates before it can be trusted.

e.g. Harden a candidate against schema + policy gates

OpenEnrichmentHub

The Enhance method — enrich an entity with cross-source attributes, embeddings, and use-cases.

e.g. Enrich an entity with cross-source attributes

OpenOptimizationHub

The Optimize method — the descent passes that remove unnecessary LLM calls and cut cost.

e.g. Run the deterministic-replacement pass to drop an LLM call

OpenVerificationHub

The Verify method — the verified-working gate a DAG must pass before it runs or serves.

e.g. Gate a DAG on verified-working before execution
